- Member state: The Netherlands
- Date issued: 17 May 2024 (the date on page 1 near "Issuing Authority: NMi Certin B.V., OIML Issuing Authority NL1" and "17 May 2024")
- OIML issuer ID: NL1

Issuing authority:
- Name: NMi Certin B.V.
- Address: Thijseweg 11, 2629 JA Delft, The Netherlands
- Person responsible: M.Ph.D. Schmidt
- Phone: +31 88 6362332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl
- oiml_issuer_id: NL1

Applicants:

Certified type:

- Type designations: IND360
- Module designation: The tables cover configurations for Digital load cells/Weighing modules interfaces (CANbus, LiNet, SICSPro) and Analog load cells (with/without ISB). Hmm, this indicator works with analog and digital load cells. The module_designation field is for e.g. "Analog load cell" for R60 certs. Here the certified type is an indicator, so module_designation should probably be null or "Not applicable". Actually the certificate covers the indicator IND360 used with analog load cells or digital load cells/weighing modules. I'll set module_designation to null.

Recommendation:
- OIML R 76-1, edition 2006. Canonical id "R76". Accuracy classes: I, II, III, IIII. But wait, accuracy classes vary per configuration: Digital (CANbus/LiNet): (III) or (IIII); SICSPro: (I), (II), (III), (IIII). Overall the certificate says "for accuracy class (I) or (II) or (III) or (IIII)". So accuracy_classes: ["I", "II", "III", "IIII"].
- Scheme: A

- NMi-2493052-01 rev 1, 2021-03-01, 56 pages

Characteristics:

Page 2 table: Digital load cells or Weighing modules (as connected peripherals), columns: CANbus interface, LiNet interface, SICSPro interface.

This is a config-level matrix: axis = "interface" (CANbus, LiNet, SICSPro).

Rows:
- Accuracy class OIML R 76: CANbus+LiNet (colspan 2): (III) or (IIII); SICSPro: (I), (II), (III) or (IIII)
- OIML R 51: CANbus+LiNet: Y(a) or Y(b), XIII(x) or XIII(2); SICSPro: Y(I), Y(II), Y(a) or Y(b), XI(x), XII(x), XIII(x) or XIII(2)
- OIML R 61: Ref(0,2) for all
- Weighing range(s): CANbus: Single interval; LiNet: Single interval, Multi-interval; SICSPro: Single interval, Multi-interval, Multiple range
- Max number of scale intervals (one weighing range): CANbus+LiNet: n ≤ 10000 divisions; SICSPro: n ≤ 1000000 divisions
- Max number of scale intervals (multi-interval or multiple range): CANbus: "-"; LiNet: n ≤ 10000 divisions (per (partial) weighing range); SICSPro: n ≤ 100000 divisions (per (partial) weighing range)
- Maximum number of weighing ranges: CANbus: 1; LiNet+SICSPro: 3
- Load cell power supply: 12 V DC (all)
- Fraction of the maximum permissible error: 0 (all) — hmm, "0"? That's odd; typically plc = 0.5 or 1. The markdown says 0. Actually for page 3 analog it says 0,5 (0.5). Page 2 says 0. Hmm, "Fraction of the maximum permissible error: 0" — that could be plc = 0? Not typical but let's record what's given. Actually wait — maybe it's "0,5" and the comma got lost? The page 3 table says 0,5. Page 2 says 0. I'll record 0 as given for digital, 0.5 for analog.
- Temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C (all)
- Climatic environment: humidity: non-condensing; intended location: Closed
- Electromagnetic environment class: E2
- Power supply voltage: 100 – 240 V AC 50/60 Hz (only for Harsh version), 20 - 28 V DC (for all versions), (not suitable for a road vehicle power supply)

This should be split:
- power_supply_voltage_ac: {min:100, max:240} V, condition: Harsh version only
- power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60} Hz
- power_supply_voltage_dc: {min:20, max:28} V
- note: not suitable for road vehicle power supply

Page 3 table: Analog load cells interface configurations.
Columns: "Analog load cells" (plain), then "Analog load cells with ISB" with 3 columns (excitation 1,5 V; 2,3 V; 3,9 V).

Structure:
- Row: "Minimum input voltage per verification scale interval": col1 (plain analog): 0,3 µV; cols 2-4 (ISB): 0,25 µV
- Row: "Load cell excitation voltage": 5 V DC | 1,5 V DC | 2,3 V DC | 3,9 V DC
- Row: "Minimum load cell resistance": 43 Ω | 43 Ω | 87 Ω | 350 Ω
- Row: "Maximum load cell resistance": 1245 Ω (all)
- Fraction of maximum permissible error: 0,5
- Load cell interface: 6-wire with sense technology, may be configured as 4-wire
- Max cable length per cross wire section: 1571 m/mm² with note
- Temperature range: -10/+40 °C
- humidity: non-condensing, location: Closed
- EMC: E2
- Power supply voltage: same as page 2

Plus 12-wire configuration text:
- minimum load cell resistance: 86 Ω
- ISB shall not be used
- max cable length per cross wire section: 433 m/mm²
- compatibility of modules form used same way as 6-wire parallel

How to model these? These are configuration-dependent: axis = "load_cell_interface_configuration" with conditions: "Analog load cells (6-wire)", "Analog load cells with ISB (1.5V excitation)", "Analog load cells with ISB (2.3V excitation)", "Analog load cells with ISB (3.9V excitation)", "12-wire connection".

I'll use config_level entries:

config_level:
- attribute: "accuracy_class_r76", axis: "load cell interface / peripheral type", values:
  Hmm, accuracy class varies by interface for digital; for analog it's (III) or (IIII) for all.

Let me structure:

Page 2 table → config_level with axis "connected peripheral interface" (CANbus / LiNet / SICSPro).

Config-level values structure: {condition, value, unit_symbol, footnote_markers}. The schema shows `{condition, value}` and rule 5 says values follow same structured form: `{condition, value, unit_symbol}`.

Let me build config entries for page 2 table:

1. attribute: "accuracy_class_oiml_r76", axis: "digital interface"
   - condition: "CANbus interface", value: "III or IIII"
   - condition: "LiNet interface", value: "III or IIII"
   - condition: "SICSPro interface", value: "I, II, III or IIII"
   Hmm, classes as strings. Value could be a string. That's fine — value can be a string.

2. attribute: "accuracy_class_oiml_r51", axis: "digital interface"
   - CANbus: "Y(a) or Y(b); XIII(x) or XIII(2)"
   - LiNet: same
   - SICSPro: "Y(I), Y(II), Y(a) or Y(b); XI(x), XII(x), XIII(x) or XIII(2)"

3. attribute: "accuracy_class_oiml_r61", axis: "digital interface" — all "Ref(0.2)". Could be type_level instead. Value "Ref(0.2)". Hmm — R61 dynamic accuracy class "Ref(0,2)". I'll record as type_level string since it applies to all. Actually it appears in both tables (digital and analog). Record as type_level: oiml_r61_class: "Ref(0.2)". Keep original comma or convert to dot? It's a designation not a decimal number — "Ref(0,2)" is the R61 accuracy class designation. I'd keep as "Ref(0,2)". Hmm, but decimal separator rule... This is a class label, not a numeric value. Keep "Ref(0,2)" as the designation. I'll keep it as-is.

4. attribute: "weighing_range_types", axis: "digital interface"
   - CANbus: "Single interval"
   - LiNet: "Single interval; Multi-interval"
   - SICSPro: "Single interval; Multi-interval; Multiple range"

5. attribute: "max_scale_intervals_single_range", axis: "digital interface"
   - CANbus: 10000 (divisions, ≤)
   - LiNet: 10000
   - SICSPro: 1000000
   value with max bound: {min: null, max: 10000}, unit: "divisions". n ≤ 10000. I'll express value as {"max": 10000, "min": null} with unit_symbol "divisions".

6. attribute: "max_scale_intervals_multi_interval_or_multiple_range", axis: "digital interface"
   - CANbus: null (not applicable, "-")
   - LiNet: {max: 10000} per partial weighing range
   - SICSPro: {max: 100000} per partial weighing range
   condition includes the note. I'll add a "note" or include in condition? The schema value shape doesn't have note. I could put the parenthetical in the condition. E.g., condition: "LiNet interface, per (partial) weighing range". Good.

7. attribute: "max_number_of_weighing_ranges", axis: "digital interface"
   - CANbus: 1
   - LiNet: 3
   - SICSPro: 3

8. attribute: "load_cell_power_supply" — type_level: 12 V DC → value 12, unit "V", plus a separate note "DC"? Rule: "110-240V AC 50/60Hz" split example includes power_supply_type. For "12 V DC": value 12, unit_symbol "V", and maybe type_level load_cell_power_supply_type: "DC". I'll do value: 12, unit_symbol: "V" and a separate attribute "load_cell_power_supply_type": "DC".

9. attribute: "fraction_of_maximum_permmissible_error" (plc) — page 2: 0 for digital; page 3: 0.5 for analog. These vary by connected-module configuration → config_level:
   - axis: "connected module type", condition "digital load cells or weighing modules (any interface)": value 0
   - condition "analog load cells": value 0.5

10. Temperature range: -10/+40 °C — type_level.

11. Climatic environment: humidity "non-condensing", intended location "Closed" — type_level.

12. EMC class E2 — type_level.

13. Power supply voltage — type_level (same on both pages):
    - power_supply_voltage_ac: {min 100, max 240} V, condition/footnote: only for Harsh version
    - power_supply_frequency: {min 50, max 60} Hz (AC)
    - power_supply_voltage_dc: {min 20, max 28} V (all versions)
    - note: not suitable for road vehicle power supply → maybe attribute "road_vehicle_power_supply_suitable": "No" or a general note. I'll include attribute "power_supply_note" with the string. Hmm, keep it simple: I'll include "power_supply_voltage_ac" with condition? type_level has single value shape {value, unit_symbol, footnote_markers}. The Harsh-version-only qualifier doesn't fit footnote markers. I could use config_level with axis "instrument version": condition "Harsh version": AC 100-240V; condition "all versions": DC 20-28V. That seems cleaner. Let me do:

    config_level:
    - attribute: "power_supply_voltage_ac", axis: "instrument version", values: [{condition: "Harsh version", value: {min:100,max:240}, unit_symbol: "V"}, ...] — only Harsh has AC.
    - attribute: "power_supply_frequency", axis: "instrument version", values: [{condition: "Harsh version (AC supply)", value: {min:50, max:60}, unit_symbol: "Hz"}]
    - attribute: "power_supply_voltage_dc", axis: "instrument version", values: [{condition: "all versions", value: {min:20, max:28}, unit_symbol: "V"}]
    - type_level: "road_vehicle_power_supply": "not suitable"

    Alternatively simpler: type_level entries with the qualifiers captured... type_level doesn't have condition. I'll use config_level as above. Good.

Page 3 table → config_level with axis "analog load cell connection":

Configurations:
- A: "Analog load cells (without ISB)" — excitation 5 V DC, min signal input voltage Umin = 0 mV, min input voltage per verification scale interval 0.3 µV, min load cell resistance 43 Ω
- B: "Analog load cells with ISB, 1.5 V excitation" — min input voltage/e 0.25 µV, min LC resistance 43 Ω
- C: "Analog load cells with ISB, 2.3 V excitation" — 0.25 µV, 87 Ω
- D: "Analog load cells with ISB, 3.9 V excitation" — 0.25 µV, 350 Ω
- E: "12-wire connection" — min LC resistance 86 Ω, no ISB, max cable length 433 m/mm²

Common to all analog: max load cell resistance 1245 Ω, plc 0.5, load cell interface 6-wire with sense technology (may be configured as 4-wire), max cable length 1571 m/mm², temperature, humidity, location, EMC, power supply.

Wait — actually the table structure: columns are "Analog load cells" | "Analog load cells with ISB" spanning 3 columns. The excitation voltage row lists 5V, 1.5V, 2.3V, 3.9V across the four columns. So the with-ISB group has 3 sub-configurations by excitation voltage. The min input voltage per verification scale interval: 0.3 µV for plain analog; 0.25 µV for all ISB columns. Min load cell resistance: 43/43/87/350.

Config-level entries:

- attribute: "load_cell_excitation_voltage", axis: "analog load cell connection", values:
  - {condition: "Analog load cells (6-wire, without ISB)", value: 5, unit_symbol: "V DC"?}. Unit: "V" with value string "5 V DC"? Better: value 5, unit_symbol "V", and maybe include DC in... I'll use unit_symbol "V" and condition mentions. Actually excitation "5 V DC" — I'll set value: 5, unit_symbol: "V DC"? Rule says unit symbol like "V". DC is the type. Hmm, for excitation voltage DC is implied; I'll put unit_symbol "V" and add nothing. Or keep "V DC" as unit_symbol — it's common. The strict rule: pull unit out. "V DC" as unit symbol is acceptable-ish but I'll use "V" to be canonical. Actually for clarity, "V DC" appears commonly. I'll use "V" for excitation and load cell power supply, since DC noted separately.

  Values: 5, 1.5, 2.3, 3.9 V for the four configurations.

  - plain analog: 0.3 µV

  - ISB 2.3V: 0.25 µV
  - ISB 3.9V: 0.25 µV

  - plain: 43 Ω

- attribute: "maximum_load_cell_resistance": 1245 Ω — applies to analog configs (all four columns). 12-wire? The text says min 86 for 12-wire; max probably still 1245. I'll record type_level? It's specific to analog load cell use. I'll record as config_level with condition "analog load cells (all configurations)" value 1245 Ω. Or type_level. Given indicator cert covering multiple connection types, config_level with axis "analog load cell connection", condition "all (6-wire and 12-wire)".

Hmm, to keep it manageable I'll record maximum_load_cell_resistance as type_level: 1245 Ω. But is it relevant to digital load cells/weighing modules? The indicator supplies 12V DC to digital load cells — resistance not applicable. It's cleaner as config-level with condition "analog load cells". I'll do config_level.

- attribute: "maximum_cable_length_per_cross_wire_section", axis: "load cell connection":
  - condition "6-wire with sense technology, indicator to junction box or load cells": value 1571, unit "m/mm²"
  - condition "12-wire, indicator to junction box": value 433, unit "m/mm²"
  Also note: if sense not used, load cells connected directly without junction box or extension cable. Add as separate note or in condition. I'll append to condition text or add footnotes? It's not a numbered footnote. I could add to characteristics as a note... The schema doesn't have notes on config values. I'll fold it into the condition: "6-wire with sense technology (indicator to junction box or load cells); without sense technology load cells connect directly without junction box or extension cable". Long but preserves info.

- attribute: "load_cell_interface": "6-wire with sense technology, may be configured as 4-wire" — config_level, condition "analog load cells".

- attribute: "intrinsic_safety_barrier (ISB)": optional; ISB used in 3 configs; not used in 12-wire. The axis conditions already capture it.

- attribute: "accuracy_class_oiml_r76", axis "analog load cell connection", all: "(III) or (IIII)". Could record but it duplicates. I'll include for completeness: values all "III or IIII". Hmm — might be noisy. The overall recommendation accuracy_classes covers I–IIII. For digital SICSPro it's I–IIII; CANbus/LiNet III/IIII. I already include accuracy_class per digital interface in config_level. For analog, add condition "analog load cells (all configurations)": "III or IIII". OK.

R51 classes for analog: Y(a) or Y(b), XIII(x) or XIII(2) — same as CANbus. Add condition "analog load cells (all configurations)". R61 Ref(0,2) — type_level across everything. Good.

Also matrix_tables for the page 2 and page 3 characteristic tables? Rule 4 example shows for R137 both matrix_tables AND model_level. Software table → matrix_tables (doesn't fit elsewhere well, though components capture it). I'll keep matrix_tables for software only.

I won't emit model_level attributes since no numeric attribute matrix by model. Actually maybe skip model_family entirely to avoid fabrication?
